question: If the resistance of a conductor is doubled while keeping the potential difference across its ends constant, what will happen to the current flowing through it?
solution:
The correct answer is __**It will halve**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

 
• The relationship between current (I), voltage (V), and resistance (R) is given by Ohm's Law: **I = V/R**.
 
• If the resistance of a conductor is doubled and the potential difference (voltage) remains constant, the current flowing through it is inversely proportional to the resistance.
